t: The Picts were the peoples of Scotland north of the Forth, united from the 6th century under powerful over-kings.
Bridei son of Beli’s victory at Dun Nechtain in 685 ended Northumbrian rule north of the Forth.
After Viking defeats in the 9th century, Picts and Gaels merged into the kingdom of Alba, the core of Scotland.
dyk: Pictish carved symbols, such as the crescent and V-rod and the double disc and Z-rod, appear on many stones across Scotland, yet their meaning has never been deciphered.
ev: A Roman panegyric first names the Picts as enemies of Britain
Picts join the 'barbarian conspiracy' against Roman Britain
Columba visits King Bridei son of Maelchon near the River Ness
Bridei son of Beli defeats and kills Ecgfrith of Northumbria at Dun Nechtain
Nechtan son of Der-Ilei expels the clergy of Iona
Óengus son of Fergus carries out the 'smiting' of Dál Riata
Vikings kill King Eóganán and many Pictish nobles
Cináed mac Ailpín becomes king of the Picts

f.capital: No fixed capital; royal centres included Burghead and later Forteviot
